summary.headline: Genus Power Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR1,524 crore; FY27 revenue guided to INR6,000-6,500 crore with EBITDA margin cut to ~18%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR1,524 crore (up 63% YoY, 36% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR284 crore (up 36%) and PAT from continuing operations of INR181 crore (up 41%). Gross margin moderated in the quarter on a higher project-business mix with elevated hardware, software and communication costs, plus forex impact on imported meter inputs. FY26 revenue reached INR4,738 crore (up 94%), EBITDA INR960 crore (20.3% margin) and PAT INR605 crore. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin down about 2-2.5 points to ~18% on raw material inflation, while net debt rose to INR1,573 crore and is expected to peak near INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: AMISP / smart metering (project business)
segments.commentary: Q4 mix shifted toward project business with higher hardware, software, communication and infrastructure content, pressuring gross margin. Order book ~INR25,173 crore, of which ~INR23,000 crore is platform-linked (~INR16,000 crore capex, rest opex) and ~INR2,000 crore is other orders (exports, gas/water meters, other AMISPs, utilities).

segments.name: O&M / annuity
segments.commentary: O&M revenue was ~INR150 crore in FY26; management expects ~INR800-900 crore per year within 2-3 years on the current order book, sustained for 5-7 years. No segment margin disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided to ~18%, down ~2-2.5 points from FY26's 20.3%, citing raw material inflation (petroleum, chips, electronics) and forex.
FY27 meter installations guided at more than 1 crore meters.
Working capital days expected to improve by another 50-75 days in FY27; working capital intensity expected to fall to ~20% of incremental revenue in FY27 and turn negative in FY28.
Operating cash flow expected roughly at par or slightly negative by end-FY27; positive operating cash flow expected in 1H FY28 (Q1/Q2).
Peak net debt expected around INR1,900-2,000 crore, with reduction from FY28.
Capex limited to routine INR10-20 crore (dies and molds); no major capex in FY27.
Further INR600-700 crore investment in the GIC joint venture platform over FY27, FY28 and Q1 FY29.
Export revenue target INR500 crore over the next 2-3 years, with meaningful export numbers expected by end-FY27.
FY28 revenue and EBITDA guidance deferred to next quarter.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity now exceeds 18 million meters annually, supporting own AMISP projects and supply to utilities and other AMISPs.
All 24 AMISP projects (awarded meter base of 3.61 crore meters) have reached operational go-live; go-live lags installation by about 2 months.
Cumulative RDSS installations reached 87 lakh meters, including ~30 lakh in Q4 FY26; crossed 1 crore meters installed under RDSS during FY26.
Routine capex only INR10-20 crore in FY27; no major capex planned.
RDSS programme timeline extended to 2028 per government revision.
demand_pricing: Management estimates 31-32 crore smart meter requirement nationally; ~15 crore tendered and ~7 crore installed; ~9 crore tenders expected in FY27 (~5 crore currently out in Haryana, MP, Punjab, Tamil Nadu).
Company claims AMISP market share of ~22-23% and more than 30% in meter manufacturing plus AMISP combined.
All contracts are fixed-price with no raw material pass-through; commodity and forex risk sits with the company.
Management declined to give order-inflow targets or average realisation per meter, citing customised products.
Bidding stance described as selective and return-focused.

qa_highlights.question: Will positive operating cash flow guidance for FY27 still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it doubts FY27 will be cash positive; expects roughly at par or slightly negative by year-end, with positive operating cash flow from 1H FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt peak and why the increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt ~INR1,500 crore now, not expected to exceed INR1,900-2,000 crore, driven by platform investments and higher working capital.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation be handled given fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: No pass-through; the FY27 EBITDA guide of ~18% already absorbs commodity, forex and chip cost pressure. Management said hardware is ~45-50% of the INR23,000 crore platform order book, to be completed in 2-2.5 years, while O&M carries no commodity exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the INR25,000 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR23,000 crore from the platform (INR16,000 crore capex, balance opex) and ~INR2,000 crore from other orders such as exports, gas/water meters, other AMISPs and utilities.

qa_highlights.question: O&M revenue trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: O&M ~INR150 crore in FY26, expected to reach ~INR800-900 crore per year in 2-3 years on the current order book; no segment margin given.

qa_highlights.question: Export and gas/water meter opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue target of INR500 crore over 2-3 years; gas metering opportunity estimated at INR35,000-36,000 crore over 3-4 years; water metering is nascent.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression to ~18% in FY27 from raw material, forex and chip cost inflation under fixed-price contracts.
Working capital and cash flow: operating cash flow still negative; debtor and inventory days must keep falling as guided.
Rising net debt toward INR2,000 crore alongside JV platform equity and loan commitments (INR600-700 crore more over the next 2 years).
Share of profit from associates fluctuated (~INR11 crore in Q3 vs ~INR4 crore in Q4), with management aggregating several entities and unclear disclosure.
Tender timing: ~9 crore meters expected in FY27 and RDSS timeline extended to 2028; order inflow targets not given.
Australia go-live expected in the next 3-6 months; management gave little detail on market size or competition.
FY28 guidance outstanding for next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, tender pipeline and FY27 revenue, but cautious on margins and cash flow: management lowered the EBITDA guide and walked back the earlier positive-cash-flow timeline to FY28. Evasive on Australia, IntelliSmart, realisation per meter, order inflow targets and segment margins.
key_quotes: We expect FY27 to mark another phase of significant scale up in project execution with the company well positioned to achieve revenue in the range of approximately INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores.
So basically, we are looking for EBITDA of 18% for this FY -- for FY27.
I doubt. We will be at par -- we are improving our cash flows on every quarter as we guided earlier that from every quarter, there will be an improvement in the cash flow, and that is happening.
So there is no pass-through in our contracts. These are all fixed price contracts.

adds.what: Manufacturing capacity exceeds 18 million meters annually (existing, no new capacity announced)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR6,000-6,500 crore (about 27-37% over FY26's INR4,738 crore, midpoint ~31%), backed by a ~INR25,173 crore order book and >1 crore meter installations planned, though no order-inflow or realisation targets were given and FY27 EBITDA margin is cut to ~18%.
